advisories.title: Two 'occupancy v2' references are not gate-prefixed in a paragraph that later prefixes three distinct occupancies.

Three occupancies are therefore in scope in one paragraph while the first two references are bare.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: The referent is determinate: the entry's register row is DR-G20, its subject is g20-fixture-corpus.v5, and only the G20 occupancy carries namedCorpusClasses[0] and namedCorpusWhenFixturesExist.dr133 — I confirmed the G23 and G10 files are cited solely for the four platform tokens. The phrasing is also a faithful carry of the frozen successor's own purpose prose, which passed dual ACCEPT. Nothing recorded is false or ambiguous on resolution, so this does not meet the bare-token defect class, which requires a token that resolves to more than one artifact.

advisories.title: The two leftover-design disclaimers use different verbs — 'close' for OBL-G20-FX-AUTHORING, 'steal' for OBL-SDK-API-RESERVED — while the dispatch constraint is 'do not close' for both.
advisories.measurement: Line 22 reads 'Does not close leftover-design of OBL-G20-FX-AUTHORING'; line 23 reads 'Does not steal leftover-design of OBL-SDK-API-RESERVED'. The dispatch says 'Do not close leftover-design of OBL-G20-FX-AUTHORING or OBL-SDK-API-RESERVED.' There is no 'Does not close' line for OBL-SDK-API-RESERVED in the disclaimer block.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: Non-closure of OBL-SDK-API-RESERVED is separately and affirmatively asserted at speaker level in the Decision paragraph ('leftover-design of OBL-SDK-API-RESERVED remains on sdk leftover-join.v6'), and the frozen successor's leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded is [] — nothing closes on adoption. 'Steal' also mirrors the successor's own registerRowNote verb ('does not steal OBL-SDK-API-RESERVED'), so the choice is fidelity to the artifact rather than a gap. The dispatch constraint is met by the Decision sentence; no attack succeeds through the wording difference.
advisories.ifEverRepaired: Add a 'Does not close leftover-design of OBL-SDK-API-RESERVED' line alongside the existing 'steal' line, keeping both verbs.

advisories.title: The entry records fixture bytes living at fixtures/g20.v2/ while the corpus it records is at version 5; the directory name now trails the artifact by three.
advisories.measurement: The entry states 'Fixture files remain at docs/coop/artifacts/fixtures/g20.v2/ with no platform subdirectory'. I confirmed the directory holds ten files and zero subdirectories. This is the COORD-level inheritance of CLAUDE-G20FX-V5-A-3, which the draft carries forward as honesty work rather than repairing.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: This is correct and deliberate, and repairing it would be the defect: the fixture bytes did not change across v3, v4 and v5, so forking a g20.v5 directory would create ten redundant copies and break frozen-predecessor discipline. The entry names the path in full rather than by a bare version token, which is the disambiguation that matters at the record level. Recording it here only so a later reader does not mistake the directory name for a stale-fixture signal.
advisories.ifEverRepaired: Nothing to repair in this entry. If the fixture bytes ever change, fork the directory at that version, not at the corpus version.
